subject: CedarPath egress handshake bottleneck — immediate mitigation & exec update
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@cedarpath.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: CedarPath Ops <ops@cedarpath.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 20:02:00 -0800
Subject: Elevated latency & 502s from CedarPath -> Redwood (started ~17:30 PST)

Rishi —

We started seeing a dramatic spike in tail latency and a 10–15% 502 error rate for inference calls hitting your hosted endpoints around 17:30 PST. The pattern looks like intermittent TCP handshakes timing out and then cascading 502s from the Redwood proxy layer. Traffic is coming out of our us-west-2 VPC over a peered path to your ingest nodes.

Quick details:
- First observed: 2026-11-26 17:31:42 PST
- Affected region: us-west-2 -> redwood-hosted-uswest
- Error sample: ~12% 502s, tail latency up to 8.2s for short text gen requests
- Packet captures attached (tcpdump) showing SYN retransmits and RST bursts on a few flows

This is customer-impacting for several of our checkout/intent flows. Can you confirm you see the same and escalate to network/infra? We need a stop-gap mitigation while your team investigates full path health.

Thanks,
Samir
Ops Lead, CedarPath

(Attachment: tcpdump-cedarpath-20261126.pcap)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Samir Rao <samir@cedarpath.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 20:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency & 502s from CedarPath -> Redwood (started ~17:30 PST)

Samir —

Thanks for the quick flag and the pcap. I see the same signal in our observability stack (spike at ~17:29 PST correlating with increased SYN retries and proxy timeouts). I’m looping in Vanessa (Customer Success) and Naomi (SRE network lead) to coordinate a joint mitigation and exec update.

Immediate plan (next 90min):
1) Naomi to validate whether this is a peering-side NAT conntrack exhaustion vs. an upstream proxy queueing issue.
2) If peering/NAT: we’ll request your network team to shift a subset of traffic to a secondary path (if available) while we clear state.
3) If proxy/balancer: we’ll roll a fast-path config to reduce queue depth for CedarPath flows and enable a short-term fallback to a lighter-weight model endpoint to preserve availability.

Can you confirm whether CedarPath can shift 20% of production traffic to an alternate egress CIDR for a 30–60 minute window? If not, we’ll prioritize a server-side fallback. I’ll send an exec summary in ~45min.

-Rishi
Senior AE, Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redwood-runtime-metrics-20261126.csv)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 20:35:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency & 502s from CedarPath -> Redwood (started ~17:30 PST)

Rishi/Vanessa —

I pulled packet traces and backend connection stats. Quick technical summary:
- Symptom: repeated TCP SYN retransmits and mid-connection RSTs from CedarPath IP ranges to our edge proxy; proxy reports increased connection queueing and intermittent upstream resets.
- Hypothesis: conntrack (NAT) tables on the peering appliance are hitting a threshold due to a burst of short-lived connections from CedarPath's new traffic pattern (spike in concurrent ephemeral ports).
- Evidence: our edge NAT counters show a large jump in conntrack active entries at 17:28–17:34 PST; clearing the conntrack table on a probe host reduced retransmits in a lab run.

Immediate actions I recommend (taking now):
A) Apply a targeted conntrack garbage-collection on the peering-facing NAT appliance (risk: 1–2s transient connection resets).
B) Temporarily pin CedarPath to a pooled set of longer-lived keepalive connections on our ingress to reduce ephemeral churn.
C) If CedarPath can route a small percentage of traffic to their secondary egress (Samir — please confirm), we’ll shift that subset immediately to reduce pressure.

Marcus, can you pre-authorize a short-lived conntrack GC window on peering (we’ll schedule for :45 PST)?

-naomi
SRE (Network), Redwood Inference

(Attachment: egress-route-map-annotated.png)

From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 20:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Elevated latency & 502s from CedarPath -> Redwood (started ~17:30 PST)

Approved. Naomi — go ahead with the targeted conntrack GC on the peering appliance at 20:45 PST. I’ll have two engineers on standby to verify connection rebuild and to roll the lighter-weight endpoint fallback if we see >5% error persistence after GC.

Operational checklist I’m executing now:
- Notify edge operators and peering NOC (done).
- Prepare a config rollback if we see unexpected mass resets (automated).
- Coordinate with CS (Vanessa) to prepare a customer-facing note for CedarPath execs post-mitigation.

Vanessa — please draft a 1-paragraph executive summary we can send to CedarPath leadership after the GC window. Keep it factual and include next steps for a longer-term permanent fix.

-Marcus
VP Infrastructure, Redwood Inference

Rishi/Team —

Thanks for the rapid coordination. We ran the traffic-shift test (moved ~25% to our secondary egress) and saw immediate restoration of tail latency for that cohort. Your conntrack GC and the fallback endpoint also reduced overall 502s to ~1.4% within 10 minutes — huge improvement.

Next asks from CedarPath:
1) Can Redwood provide a short post-mortem with the timeline and the root cause hypothesis (peering NAT conntrack exhaustion) and a permanent remediation plan?
2) We’d like to schedule a technical working session next week with your SRE and our network team to discuss long-term fixes (pooling, keepalives, or dedicated peering sizing).

Appreciate the clear comms. Please send exec note and PM with available time slots for the working session.

—Samir
Ops Lead, CedarPath
